messages:
andrea: Heads-up — noticed sustained memory growth on Dedicated pool when serving long contexts (~10k tokens). KV cache resident size keeps climbing; it doesn't reclaim after sessions finish. Anyone else seeing this?

samir: I hit something similar yesterday on a Dedicated v2 cluster (A100). Hosted traces looked fine. Could be an env/config drift.

jules: Added a quick perf run — seeing a lot of minor pagefaults during compaction cycles. Allocator keeps mapping new pages instead of reusing freed ranges.

miko: Hypothesis: kernel selection + mmap flags differ across environments. Onprem images have hugetlb and specific madvise patterns; Hosted/Dedicated might fall back to different kernel paths. VPC containers also have cgroup tunables that affect mmap/compaction.

samir: Do we have the profile clips or repro steps?

andrea: Dropping the perf snippet I grabbed from Dedicated canary (trimmed):

```
# perf top -p <pid>
  23.4% kv_compact_shard
  12.1% kv_insert
  10.3% page_fault_handler
  8.7% arena_alloc
# dmesg tail
[12345.678] vm: page allocation failure: order:0, mode:0x8000
[12345.679] OOM killer invoked? none
```

jules: Also saw the kv_free_segments metric trending down while total_alloc grew. Largest_free_chunk reduced from ~1.2G -> ~120M over the run. Fragmentation looks real.

ops-eli: On Dedicated our container runtime enforces a softer memory limit (memory.swap.max is high). Private onprem uses hugetlb and strict cgroup memory.max. That difference could change how the allocator handles returning pages to the kernel vs keeping them.

miko: Another angle: batching heuristics. Our continuous-batching can keep contexts alive longer (microbatches touching KV), which prevents eviction of entries and increases resident set. If Dedicated's kernel fallback uses MADV_DONTNEED differently, we get different reclaim behavior.

samir: Can you share the exact reproducer command you used?

jules: Repro command we used in the canary: 
```
./tools/run_infer --model redwood/xxl --context 12000 --stream false --batch 1 --profile kv --duration 15m
```
Logs (abbreviated):
```
[00:02] kv_entries=1.4M kv_resident=6.8G kv_free_segments=2048 largest_free=128M
[00:08] kv_entries=1.8M kv_resident=9.1G kv_free_segments=700 largest_free=64M
[00:12] kv_entries=2.0M kv_resident=11.0G kv_free_segments=210 largest_free=32M
```

andrea: For Private onprem we tried MALLOC_CONF=narenzo:oversize:1,lg_chunk:20 and saw earlier compaction but also more CPU cycles. NUMA layout matters — when the process is pinned to single socket fragmentation increased faster.

miko: Quick mitigation ideas: reduce kv_ttl (default 60s -> 20s), lower max_batch_time to avoid long-lived microbatches, enable aggressive compact (kv_compact_interval=300s -> 60s) and toggle pinned allocator for onprem.

samir: If we toggle "force_optimized_kernels" to true across Dedicated/Hosted/Private in the runtime, we can see if kernel choice is the primary factor. We should run that before changing production defaults.

ops-eli: I'll prepare a canary job template that flips force_optimized_kernels and the kv settings for Dedicated pools. Also check container memory swap and hugetlb stats.

jules: One more datapoint: CI replayed the same workload with v0.9.3 runtime and didn't reproduce memory growth — regression looks introduced around v0.9.7 where we changed default mmap flags for kernel-optimized kernels.

miko: That aligns. The mmap flag change introduced on v0.9.5 caused fallback path to use MADV_FREE_REUSABLE on some kernels. Some hypervisors don't implement it well.

andrea: Plan: (1) run canary with force_optimized_kernels=true on Dedicated and Hosted, (2) run canary with kv_ttl=20s + kv_compact_interval=60s, (3) capture perf and allocator histograms, (4) test on Private onprem NUMA pinned node. I'll run 1 & 2 this afternoon and paste graphs.

ci-bot: Automated test run queued: https://ci.redwood.dev/runs/9321 (includes kv-repro harness, will upload flamegraphs).

miko: I'll open an engineering ticket to track config drift and kernel differences (RINF-4321).

ops-eli: FYI: when you run the Private onprem test, set net.core.rmem_max / wmem_max higher and check MTU alignment — weirdly we saw higher pagefaults with mismatched MTU once.

andrea: ack. I'll post results here when canaries finish. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
